INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #4
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting.

2. When practising Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills.

3. When practising Writing 2.3.1 Social Writing - Email, which approach is best? (1 mark)

5. In INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Only memorise without using the language
   B. Avoid speaking to classmates
   C. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   D. Mix random languages with no purpose

6. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Comprehension.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Comprehension.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Listening for Comprehension.

7. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Reading for Comprehension: Poetry, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Reading for Comprehension: Poetry.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Reading for Comprehension: Poetry.

   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 3.3.1 Creative Writing – Poetry.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 3.3.1 Creative Writing – Poetry.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 3.3.1 Creative Writing – Poetry.

9. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.

   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Comprehension.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
12. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 3.3.1 Creative Writing – Poetry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Conversation skills- Negotiation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 4.3.1 Essay writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
